ai.description: *Minervarya teraiensis* is a small frog (30–45 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale vertebral stripe. It features prominent, broken longitudinal skin ridges and a distinct dark mask.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya teraiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and elevated glandular fold (dorsolateral fold) running along its back.
ai.habitat: The Terai Wart Frog inhabits moist grasslands, agricultural fields, and forest edges across the Indo-Gangetic plains, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Terai Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects near water bodies and damp, grassy habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya teraiensis* reproduces via external fertilization, laying clutches of 200–500 eggs in stagnant water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya teraiensis* inhabits the Himalayan foothills and Terai regions of northern India and Nepal, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.callDescription: The Terai Wart Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "chick-chick" pulses, typically heard emanating from shallow, stagnant pools and flooded rice paddies.
